$schema_note: Hand-curated record of what ForgePact's boss soul pieces (ForgePact#197) rely on, NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file, and hs_game_sdk/soul_piece_model.py never reads it; tests/test_soul_piece_model.py reads both, checks the shared `cases` against the model and its own transforms of ForgePact's code, and (ParityTests, where ForgePact is checked out) pins ForgePact/plugin/include/ForgePact/SoulPieceMod.hpp's constants, seeds, base, act table with boss rooms, room rules and verdict words to this file. The mechanism, in our own words, is docs/models/soul-piece-spec.md; the game facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21 and § 18.4; the act of each room is hs-game-sdk/curated/room_acts.json. A `status` is one of `static_reading` (read from the compiled game and paraphrased, no script text), `inference` (follows from static readings, not read directly), `owner_named` (the owner's decision, not a reading), `our_code` (ForgePact's own choice), `measured` (a live session read it; `capture` names the session's capture, a local file the hub does not track), `unverified` (a plausible value no session has read) or `pending` (a live check of ForgePact#197 fills it). A `source` is `<path> § <section>`, the path relative to the hub root and the section text appearing in that file. `seed_base` + act is a piece's seed `a`; `reserved_seeds` are other ForgePact items' seeds a piece must never take. `base` is the game item a piece is made of: the repository entry of that name in that category, resolved by name at run time, of that class, `c` and `j`. `gem` is the Gem of Incarnation whose `droprate.base` G ForgePact reads at run time by repository name; `ratio` makes the piece's denominator D = max(1, floor(G x numerator / denominator)), 0 (no piece) for G unknown, zero or negative. `acts` is one row per act: the boss object its room is expected to bring out (an hs_game_sdk object name, with the SDK's index), the piece's name, the act's boss room (an hs_game_sdk room name, with the SDK's index) where a piece takes the player, `named` (false would make the act drop nothing and move nobody) and the row's evidence. `transfer` is how a piece moves the player there: the game scripts ForgePact calls by their hs_game_sdk names, in order (no portal object, no offset). `room_rules` are the name rules that refuse a room on top of the act table, each with the verdict word it gives. `drop_verdicts` and `use_verdicts` are the words, in the order ForgePact asks them; `force_overrides` the drop verdicts `soulpiece force on` may replace with `hit`. `cases` are shared inputs and their expected answer: `drop` (DecideDrop; `act` is the room's act, 0 for none) and `use` (DecideUse; `act` is the room's act, 0 for none, and a `transfer` case names the boss room it leads to) are ForgePact's; `stack` is the game's stack rule (soul_piece_model.stacks) for an item `picked` up beside a `held` one, each `{t: class, b, c, a: seed}`, where a `b` other than the base's 12 stands for any definition of that class. A roll is uniform in [0, 1). `open_questions` are the questions about the game the live procedures answer (and the ones no session can), each with the live check that answers it, its `answer` once a session ran it, and the model's HYPOTHESES key where it decides one.

transfer.reset_source: docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.6 Zone state and a boss room's return
transfer.note: The owner, after Live procedure 3: a direct transfer, no portal. NetworkRoomGoto(<boss room>) with the player as self took the player to Act_01_Boss and Act_02_Boss (goto-travel), where the room's Pentagram_Boss_obj brought out the boss; a Portal_obj whose portalZone record held the boss room took the player to the zone's ordinary next zone instead (portal-travel and portal-travel-2 failed). Before the travel, ZoneStateExists(<boss room>) is asked for the fresh count and ZoneStateResetSingle(<boss room>) drops the room's saved zone state whatever it answered, so the boss comes out again after a kill (a static reading; Live procedure 2's on-reentry-boss measures it). Only the boss room's entry is touched, never the current room's: a use inside a boss room is refused. The call's own controls (our_code): ZoneStateExists is asked again after the reset (cleared counts a saved entry that is gone after it), a failed ZoneStateExists or ZoneStateResetSingle call is counted zone-call-failed and the transfer still goes ahead, and the status line asks ZoneStateExists for the room the player left (left, leftsaved), an ordinary zone just left being the positive control.

room_rules.note: A room drops pieces when RoomActIndex gives it an act and no rule refuses it; towns refuse first, then the boss-room rules. A use transfers from any room with an act, towns included, and is refused (the piece kept) in a room with no act and by the boss-room rules.

use_rules.action: right-click the piece in the backpack and confirm
use_rules.note: Every verdict but transfer is a refusal: PotionUse answers false and the game keeps the piece. On transfer PotionUse answers true and the game clears the piece's cell itself, as it does for the Edible PAS Logo (Live procedure 3's use-takes-one), and the next frame tick carries the transfer out. The base's own PotionUse is never called for a piece while ForgePact is installed (no-base-effect).
